Flood of Noah
fluhd uhv NOH-uh
noun
From Hebrew mabbul (H3999, a flood, deluge) and the name Noach (H5146, rest); the worldwide deluge of Genesis 6-9 by which God judged the earth.

Biblical Definition

The flood of Noah is the historical, worldwide deluge by which the LORD judged a world grown wholly corrupt and violent, while sovereignly preserving eight souls in the ark He commanded Noah to build (Gen 6-9). The Reformed faith receives the account as true history, not legend, for our Lord Jesus Christ Himself appealed to the days of Noah as a real and coming pattern of judgment (Matt 24:37-39), and the apostle Peter twice grounds doctrine upon it as literal fact. God saw that the wickedness of man was great and that every imagination of his heart was only evil continually, a stark testimony to total depravity. Yet Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD, and being warned of God moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house, by which faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith (Heb 11:7). The flood is rich in typology. Peter teaches that the eight souls saved by water are the figure of baptism (1 Pet 3:20-21), the waters of judgment becoming the waters of salvation for those in the ark, even as the believer is saved through union with the death and resurrection of Christ. Peter further teaches that as the old world perished by water, so the present heavens and earth are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment (2 Pet 3:5-7). The flood thus preaches both the certainty of final judgment and the safety of all hidden in Christ, the true ark.

Webster 1828 Definition

The historical worldwide deluge of Genesis 6-9 by which God judged the world and saved eight souls in the ark, a type of baptism and final judgment.

FLOOD OF NOAH, noun. From Hebrew mabbul (H3999, a deluge) and Noach (H5146, rest); the worldwide flood of Genesis 6-9.

A true and universal judgment upon a world grown corrupt and filled with violence.

Eight souls were saved in the ark, the figure of baptism according to the apostle Peter.

As it is written, 'By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house' (Heb 11:7).

The old world perished by water; the present world is reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

Key Scripture

Gen 6:5 — "And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually."

1Pe 3:20 — "Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water."

2Pe 3:6 — "Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished:"

Heb 11:7 — "By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith."

Modern Corruption

The flood is corrupted when treated as mere myth or as a local event, denying the worldwide judgment our Lord and His apostles affirmed as history.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The longstanding assault is to demote the flood from history to folklore, or to shrink it to a local Mesopotamian inundation. But the Lord Jesus appealed to the days of Noah as a real and coming reality, and Peter grounds the certainty of final judgment upon the literal fact that the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.

The principle to recover is the unity of judgment and salvation in the flood. The waters that drowned the rebellious world bore the ark and its eight souls to safety, which Peter names the figure of baptism. As surely as the flood came, fire is reserved for the present heavens and earth, and the only safety in either is to be hidden in Christ, the true ark, by the righteousness which is by faith.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mabbul (H3999) and Noach (H5146) name the deluge and the man through whom God preserved eight souls.

expand to see more

Hebrew mabbul (H3999) — the flood, the deluge, used uniquely of Noah's waters

Hebrew Noach (H5146) — Noah, 'rest' or 'comfort,' the preacher of righteousness

Hebrew tebah (H8392) — the ark, the vessel of salvation through the waters

Greek kataklusmos (G2627) — cataclysm, the New Testament term for the flood (Matt 24:38)

The eight souls saved by water are the figure of baptism and a type of final judgment by fire

Usage

"The flood of Noah was a true worldwide judgment, as the Lord Jesus Himself affirmed."

"Eight souls were saved through the waters, the figure of baptism and the safety of the ark."

"As the old world perished by water, the present world is reserved unto fire."
